findings.name: essentia.js - npm registry metadata
findings.claim: essentia.js is AGPL-3.0 and last published 2021-06-24.
findings.design_implication: Excluded: AGPL in the tree of an MIT npm package.

findings.name: Meyda audio features / npm 5.6.3
findings.claim: Meyda is MIT with offline extraction, MFCC and chroma but no raw mel bands; last release 2024-04-21.
findings.design_implication: Usable for spectral scalars; the mel filterbank is still ours to write.

findings.name: TensorFlow.js API signal namespace; fft.js npm
findings.claim: tfjs ships stft/frame/hannWindow but no mel filterbank op; fft.js is a MIT radix-4 FFT.
findings.design_implication: Skip the tensor runtime; take the FFT from fft.js and write ~200 lines of DSP.

findings.name: Web Audio API 1.1 s1.8.5-1.8.6 AnalyserNode
findings.claim: AnalyserNode mandates a Blackman window, 0.8 default smoothing, and reads only the most recent fftSize frames (max 32768).
findings.design_implication: AnalyserNode is excluded from the analysis path; compute the STFT over the rendered AudioBuffer.

findings.name: librosa.filters.mel vs torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram defaults
findings.claim: librosa's mel default is htk=False, norm='slaney'; torchaudio's is mel_scale='htk', norm=None.
findings.design_implication: Expose melScale and norm explicitly in the tool schema and pin them.

findings.name: MelSpectrogram inconsistency with librosa melspectrogram (pytorch/audio #1058)
findings.claim: The librosa/torchaudio mel mismatch is a filed real-world bug class.
findings.design_implication: Pick one reference (pinned librosa) and generate goldens from it.

findings.name: whisper/audio.py log_mel_spectrogram
findings.claim: Whisper's log-mel uses Hann/n_fft 400/hop 160, power, log10, a peak-relative clamp at max-8, then (x+4)/4.
findings.design_implication: Peak-relative dB changes every value when a clip is trimmed; record ref explicitly.

findings.name: librosa.power_to_db (0.11)
findings.design_implication: Tests use ref=1.0, top_db=null; peak-relative dB is display-only.

findings.name: MIT JS building blocks for mel and CQT
findings.claim: meljs 1.0.2 (NeMo-calibrated mel), cqt-web 1.0.4 (librosa-compatible CQT, WASM), wavedraw 2.7.0 (Node WAV + mel render) are all MIT.
findings.design_implication: Read as reference implementations; meljs's NeMo constants would break librosa parity if vendored unchecked.

findings.name: audio-analysis-mcp
findings.claim: An existing audio-analysis MCP server (librosa + matplotlib) saves visual outputs to disk and returns paths.
findings.design_implication: Precedent for path + numbers; match this repo's view_scored_piano_roll shape (path + inline image + summary).

findings.name: OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob(); pngjs 7.0.0; sharp 0.35.4
findings.claim: convertToBlob produces PNG in every browser and in Workers; pngjs is pure-JS MIT; sharp is a native binary.
findings.design_implication: Raster PNG is the render target; a 30 s clip at 10 ms hop is 384,000 cells, so rect-per-cell SVG is out.

findings.name: Standard MIDI Files 1.1
findings.claim: SMF times a sung line as integer ticks × microseconds-per-quarter, not BPM.
findings.design_implication: startSec is the integral of that map; a duration sentence in a prompt is not a clock.

findings.name: Intuitive Analysis of Song Structure
findings.claim: pretty_midi exists because MIDI ticks are unusable in Python; notes are pitch + start + end in seconds.
findings.design_implication: jam-sessions ScoreNote.startSec is already the lingua franca.

findings.name: music21: A Toolkit for Computer-Aided Musicology
findings.claim: music21 is the Python object graph of a score.
findings.design_implication: Python Streams, not SuperCollider or MIDI hex, are what an LLM emits correctly.

findings.name: librosa: Audio and Music Signal Analysis in Python
findings.claim: librosa analyzes audio; it does not specify a score.
findings.design_implication: DSP features recover a performance; they cannot author New Britain.

findings.name: ChatMusician
findings.claim: LLMs emit more valid music as Python/ABC than as MIDI-like tokens; free audio prompts fail the grid.
findings.design_implication: Python emits chords/beats/seconds; the model fills timbre.

findings.name: REMI
findings.claim: Without a beat-bar grid, sequence models drift; singing models consume phoneme × MIDI × duration.
findings.design_implication: sing in 35 seconds has nothing to scale.
